text:
alex: Kicking off a bring-up for a new lightweight GPU cluster in ap-south-1 (tag: ap-south-1-lite). Plan is to reuse the existing tf/pulumi region modules but we need clear state wiring + CI changes for per-region isolation. Looking for 👀 on backend suggestions and an acceptance checklist.

priya: Do we have the KMS/route53 constraints documented for that region? I remember ap-south had different KMS key alias rules and a limit on hosted zone creations. If we hit those we should fail-fast in CI.

jamie: Past lessons: pulumi state lock failed because the S3 backend was created in a different region than the bucket endpoint we used. Recommend explicit backend config with region and force_destroy off. Example: 
```
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket = "rwd-infra-state"
    key    = "ap-south-1-lite/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "ap-south-1"
    dynamodb_table = "rwd-terraform-locks"
  }
}
```
Also make sure the bucket has lifecycle + encryption policy before we run.

tony: For terraform workspaces we should use a workspace per environment (prod/stage) and a state prefix per region. Use `terraform workspace select -or-create ap-south-1-lite` in the CI job. Backend prefix snippet: 
```
backend "s3" {
  bucket = "rwd-infra-state"
  key    = "${env.workspace}/${var.region}/terraform.tfstate"
  region = "ap-south-1"
}
```
This keeps state separate and makes handoffs easier.

sara: CI changes I'll add to the GH Actions workflow: ensure S3 bucket + DynamoDB lock exist, then `terraform init -backend-config` with explicit region + table, then `terraform plan -var region=ap-south-1 -out plan.tfplan`. Also gating: require `approve-ops` label before apply. Minimal snippet: 
```yaml
- name: Init TF
  run: |
    terraform init -backend-config="bucket=$TF_STATE_BUCKET" -backend-config="key=$WORKSPACE/$REGION/terraform.tfstate" -backend-config="region=$REGION" -backend-config="dynamodb_table=$LOCK_TABLE"
- name: Plan
  run: terraform plan -var "region=$REGION" -out plan.tfplan
```

eng-ci-bot: automated-check: infra-lint: ok, module-versions: ok, k8s-schema-check: warn (compat matrix for k8s <=1.26 on this module).

priya: GPU quota note: ap-south-1 has soft limits for A10/A100; we should open tickets with cloud rep now. Estimate for initial pool: 8x A10 (spot allowed) — cost ballpark ~ $X/day — anyone object? Also we need to decide on on-demand fallback policy.

jamie: Post-bootstrap verification steps I propose: 
- `kubectl get nodes -o wide` (check GPU labels)
- `kubectl describe node <node>` (driver plugin status)
- `nvidia-smi` run via a DaemonSet job to validate GPUs
- confirm `kubelet` logs for no OOM/driver restarts: `kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/nvidia-driver-installer`
- make sure the autoscaler respects PodPriority for inference workloads.

alex: Agree with that verification list. Handoff checklist for solutions/infra: 
- backend bucket + dynamodb table created and verified 
- KMS key + alias available and documented 
- quota ticket created + approval noted 
- CI workflow updated and smoke plan passes in staging 
- cost estimate + owner assigned to monitor first 72h 
- run the post-bootstrap verification and attach logs to the ticket 
If all green we flip `region-ready` tag and notify Platform.

tony: Small extra: add a terraform `null_resource` that runs a basic k8s smoke test after apply (with retry/backoff) so CI can gate on cluster readiness. Keeps human handoffs smoother.

priya: I'll start the cloud quota request now and add KMS key creation to the infra module PR.

jamie: I'll open a PR updating the pulumi wrapper to accept `region` and `state_prefix` env vars, plus doc comments about S3 region.

ops-bot: ACTIONS CREATED: #infra-1930 (quota request), #infra-1931 (state backend update PR), #infra-1932 (ci workflow for ap-south-1-lite). Assigned: priya, jamie, sara. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks all — tagging this for handoff after PRs land. I'll post the final runbook link once I've merged the checklist into the runbooks/region-bootstrap page. :rocket:
